notice: The northern coast over time for Grind Strat (Sweden, Åland, Finland, Estonia): where the sea stood higher against today's land since AD 1219, 500 m cells. An estimate: today's land uplift (NKG_RF17vel) bent to fit dated shores from local studies, over GEBCO's heights. Shared under CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Sources: NKG_RF17vel land-uplift model © Nordic Geodetic Commission (NKG) (CC BY 4.0, creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); GEBCO Compilation Group (2026) GEBCO 2026 Grid (doi:10.5285/4f68d5c7-45eb-f999-e063-7086abc036fa) (Public domain (GEBCO Grid terms of use), dap.ceda.ac.uk/bodc/gebco/global/gebco_2026/GEBCO_Grid_terms_of_use.pdf); Made with Natural Earth (Public domain, www.naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use/). Not for navigation. Not endorsed by GEBCO, the IHO or the IOC. Made available as is.

sgu.note: SGU's shore model is not here: resource.sgu.se is not allowed yet (run with --fetch-sgu once it is). Sweden uses the estimate, bent to fit Stockholm.

regions.name: Stockholm and Lake Mälaren
regions.error: Fitted to Söderlund's 2 m about 1300, so about 2.2 m in 1219; other sources allow up to about 4.3 m. The shore could lie further inland than drawn. When Mälaren became a lake is dated only 'about 1200' to 'about 1300' (TO CHECK); at 500 m the Stockholm straits are narrower than a cell, so the build reports when Mälaren is cut off.

regions.name: North Uppland (Forsmark)
regions.error: Fitted to Eckarfjärden (5.5 m about 1100): within about 0.5 m there.

regions.name: Åland and south-west Finland (Turku)
regions.error: No control point of their own: Turku is more than 150 km from every control place, so the rule is used as it is there (k = 1, about 4.3 m in 1219); Mariehamn is just inside the reach of Stockholm and north Uppland and is bent a little (k about 0.96, about 4.6 m). A Turku curve seen only as a snippet (Vuorela et al. 2009, about 3.8 mm a year) suggests about 3 m: the shore may be drawn too far inland. TO CHECK. Turku and Åland also sit on GEBCO's 60°N seam, where the land heights change source.

regions.name: Gulf of Finland, north coast (Helsinki to Vyborg)
regions.error: Mostly k = 1, nearer Tallinn bent towards Tallinn's fit. About 2.8 m at Helsinki in 1219, no control point: about ±1 m.

regions.name: North Estonia (Tallinn)
regions.error: Fitted to Harku (2.73 m about 910) and Saarse and Vassiljev's linear shore line (2.0 m in 1219): within about 0.6 m.

regions.name: West Estonia and the islands (Haapsalu, Hiiumaa, Saaremaa, Pärnu)
regions.error: Fitted to Salme (about 1 m in 1219, from an abstract only). The land is very flat here, so a few decimetres of error move the shore by hundreds of metres; GEBCO's whole-metre heights and tree tops make it worse. Haapsalu and Pärnu lie between Salme and Tallinn and take a blend of the two.

regions.name: Gulf of Riga, Kurzeme and the south coast
regions.error: The sea fell less than 0.5 m since 1219 (Riga about 0.3 m), below what whole-metre heights can show, so nothing changes; further south the sea was if anything slightly lower than today (HOLSEA brackets at Puck: between about -1.24 and -0.64 m around 1150-1250), which is left to hand-drawn fixes.
